meta.title: Konrad Thiemann · Software Engineer
meta.description: Software engineer focused on frontend. I build considered, lean and documented solutions – in production e-commerce and my own projects, with AI as a deliberately built tool.

hero.tagline: A software engineer who builds deliberately.
hero.intro: I build things that make people's lives easier – and in a way a team can build on: considered, lean, documented. I use frameworks and AI as a deliberate choice, not out of habit.

items.title: I question before I build.
items.desc: Before adopting a solution, I check whether it really fits the problem. That's how I came to shape 110+ UI building blocks of an in-house library that replaces a third-party framework – leaner and faster.

items.title: I build purpose-fit, not bloated.
items.desc: Lean, targeted solutions over universal heavyweights: fewer dependencies, clearer responsibilities, better performance.

items.title: Quality is built in – and lived.
items.desc: Automated quality gates (lint → typecheck → test → build) and traceable commits – so a team can keep building fast and safely.

items.title: I enable others.
items.desc: Apprentice, intern or team – I share knowledge instead of hoarding it. Including how to use AI sensibly in everyday development.

experience.title: What I own at work
experience.lead: For almost three years I've worked on the frontend of a multi-brand e-commerce system – today across four brands. I look after not just the shop but the system around it – across eight subsystems. I think *in connections*, not isolated tasks.
items: Shop plus a direct-order-pages variant
Helped build a custom UI library that replaces a third-party framework
API and GraphQL layer, shared libraries & drop-in packages
Strapi CMS
Technical SEO: automated sitemaps, meta data & Google Discover optimisation
Noticeably faster load times through targeted performance work
Security hardening for business-critical applications: Content Security Policy, XSS and open-redirect protection
Technical groundwork for the ongoing migration to Shopify Plus
experience.educationDesc: Intensive web developer training focused on modern frontend development.

items.text: His keen grasp of new topics, above-average commitment and strong willingness to learn – combined with excellent communication skills and the ability to think critically – set him apart.
He carries out all tasks entirely independently, with great care and thorough planning. He always acts calmly, thoughtfully, with focus and the utmost precision.
Konrad is an exceptional career changer, whose ability to learn and grow quickly impressed me deeply.
The decision to hire Konrad was one of the best I have ever made, and I would make it again without hesitation.
I can recommend Konrad without reservation to any team or company that values committed, fast learners and authentic personalities.
In just over two years, Konrad grew from a career changer into one of our most important software developers.
On his own initiative, Konrad designed AI-assisted development workflows for our team, standardising and speeding up our processes.

ai.title: AI – deliberately built
ai.body: I don't reach for AI at random – I deliberately define how it works: a system of specialised AI agents with clearly documented workflows. At work and in my own projects I steer the AI tooling through dedicated configuration files.
ai.note: AI with *high leverage*, not blind trust.

tech.note: Tools and technologies I work with every day.

projects.title: What I build
projects.note: Personal projects – for learning, experimenting and the joy of building.

doewe.name: Doewe
doewe.detail: A platform for logging expenses, setting budgets and tracking financial goals. Full-stack with Next.js, TypeScript, Prisma and PostgreSQL – strictly typed, with CI and tests.

pokemeta.name: Pokékon
pokemeta.tagline: Tournament data, deck tracking and AI analysis for the TCG meta.
pokemeta.detail: A dashboard for the Pokémon TCG meta: tournament data, multi-deck management and AI-assisted battle-log analysis. Originally built local-first (IndexedDB), currently in deliberate migration to a server API (Hono, PostgreSQL) as the single source of truth – the architecture decision is documented openly, not hidden.

prized.name: Prized
prized.detail: A training mini-game for trading card games: guess the six hidden prize cards by process of elimination. PWA with stat tracking, Supabase auth for guests and registered users, and a multi-tier card-image fallback for high availability.

fotochallenge.name: Foto-Challenge
fotochallenge.tagline: Scan a QR code, complete a task, create a memory.
fotochallenge.detail: A party and wedding app: guests scan a QR code and get assigned a photo challenge from 219 curated tasks. Password-protected gallery, installable PWA with an offline shell – deliberately built with no sign-up friction for guests.

waldbingo.name: Waldbingo
waldbingo.detail: Family bingo with cards generated based on weather and location as a web app, plus a standalone Python generator for print-ready PDF bingo cards – motivation to head outside and explore your surroundings.

aiinfra.name: Agentic Infra Dashboard
aiinfra.tagline: My AI engineering infrastructure, made visible live.
aiinfra.detail: A meta-dashboard over my own agentic-engineering setup: every repo, the global Claude Code agents, skills, rules and hooks, and the workflows they form – including monitoring of TDD-gate blocks and per-repo CI status. Keeps itself current via a hook-driven data branch, with no redeploy needed.

teaching.title: Sharing knowledge
teaching.lead: What I know, *I pass on* – within the team and beyond.
items: Taught our apprentice how to code
Ran internal trainings on programming with AI
Guest on the developAkademie podcast

about.title: About me
about.body: *Software engineer* – currently working mainly in frontend, but not defined by it. I build software that makes people's lives easier, and I keep mature e-commerce systems running and evolving. I deliberately invest in good tools – including the way I use AI.

personal.title: Beyond code
personal.note: Two hobbies, the same way of thinking as programming – expand for the connection.

hobbies.title: Skateboarding
hobbies.tagline: Fall, correct, try again – until the trick lands.
hobbies.detail: Every trick follows the same path: countless failed attempts, small corrections, until the movement clicks. Sports neuroscience shows this kind of repeated, focused practice measurably reshapes the cerebellum and keeps the brain in a constant state of neuroplasticity. The same love of iteration – try, learn from the failure, try again – is what I bring to programming.

hobbies.title: Competitive Pokémon TCG
hobbies.tagline: Reading a board, not memorising 60 cards.
hobbies.detail: Someone who reads a board quickly isn't seeing 60 individual cards – they're seeing familiar configurations. That's the same “chunking” cognitive science has documented in experts since Chase and Simon's chess studies (1973), later confirmed in fields like radiology, aviation and business forecasting. That exact pattern-recognition-over-memorising is how I read code: familiar bug and architecture patterns jump out, instead of calculating every line from scratch.

meta.title: Konrad Thiemann · AI System
meta.description: How I use AI in software development: rules, skills, agents and hooks as one continuous, automatically enforced system.

hero.label: AI Setup
hero.intro: I don't use AI in development ad hoc – I run it through a deliberately built system of four building blocks: rules, skills, agents and hooks. Each takes on a different job – together they form a traceable, automatically enforced workflow, at work and in my own projects alike.
hero.dashboardCta: See it live in the Agentic Infra Dashboard

pillars.title: Four building blocks, one system
pillars.lead: Each building block plays a different role in the same flow – from silent convention to automated enforcement.

items.title: Rules
items.desc: Baseline conventions that apply automatically in every repo – I don't have to repeat them in every prompt. One CLAUDE.md per workspace level, plus dedicated rule files per topic.
items: Code style — TS strict, PSR-12/Symfony, Vue SFC conventions
Git & commits — branch names, Conventional Commits, PR format
Security & secrets — Keychain instead of plaintext, no real keys in public repos
Spec-driven development — spec first, then plan, then code
Test-driven development — red-green-refactor is mandatory
Worktrees — parallel agents without file collisions

items.title: Skills
items.desc: Recurring workflows I trigger with a command instead of explaining them every time. “/feature” chains the others into one complete flow.
items: /feature — chains spec → plan → tests → implementation → gates → review
/spec — writes the spec (problem, user stories, acceptance criteria)
/commit — a Conventional Commit in the workspace format
/worktree — sets up an isolated worktree for parallel work
/new-app — repo scaffold including CI and commit setup
/wrap-session — a structured close-out for a work session

items.title: Agents
items.desc: Specialised roles with their own toolset that I use deliberately for individual steps, instead of handing one model everything at once.
items: orchestrator — breaks down multi-layer features, coordinates the other agents
planner — implementation plan incl. interfaces & contracts, writes no code
tester — writes failing tests from the plan's contracts (red)
implementer — makes tests pass, sticks to the quality gates
reviewer — checks diffs for real defects, not style
security — audits auth, input handling and secrets before shipping
data-analyst — schema, migration and query planning
docs — keeps README, changelog and docs in sync with the code

items.title: Hooks
items.desc: Automated enforcement running in the background – not relying on discipline, but technically blocking whatever violates my own rules.
items: git-safety — blocks force-push, pushing to main, reset --hard, .env commits
tdd-gate — blocks git commit without a green test run, PR creation without lint/typecheck/test
infra-dashboard-sync — keeps the Agentic Infra Dashboard current automatically
stop-notify — notifies me when an agent run finishes

flow.title: How a feature moves through the system
flow.lead: Using a non-trivial feature as the example – kicked off with a single command.

steps.title: Write the spec
steps.desc: Problem, user stories and testable acceptance criteria – before anything gets built. I sign off on the spec before it moves forward.

steps.title: Create the plan
steps.desc: A layer-by-layer plan with interfaces & contracts. No code – just the decisions tester and implementer need as a binding baseline.

steps.title: Write tests (red)
steps.desc: Failing tests written directly from the plan's contracts – without knowing the implementation.

steps.title: Implement (green)
steps.desc: Makes the tests pass, nothing more. Sticks to code-style and security rules.

steps.title: Enforce the gate
steps.desc: The commit is technically blocked if no green test run has been detected since the last change – regardless of whether I forget.

steps.title: Review against the spec
steps.desc: Checks the diff for real defects and against the spec's acceptance criteria – not for taste.

flow.note: For one-liners or trivial fixes I run this flow myself, without the full agent apparatus – the system scales with the task, not against it.
